description: Claude Desktop DOM selector contract with precision selectors verified against actual DOM structure. Selectors target known CSS class patterns, testids, and semantic elements.

verifiedAgainst.note: Selectors verified against Claude Desktop DOM snapshots. Class names use CSS Modules prefix matching where hash varies.

scopeVocabulary.all: All routes (home / thread) plus overlay elements (menu / dialog)
scopeVocabulary.home: Home/welcome screen with suggestions and input
scopeVocabulary.thread: Conversation/thread view with messages and markdown
scopeVocabulary.config: Elements that only appear with user configuration (e.g., project selector)

selectors.notes: Main content surface. First match used. Claude Desktop may use main.main-surface or generic main element.
Left sidebar/navigation panel. May be removed and rebuilt on toggle — never clear skin when it disappears.
Top header bar. Must not override position/z-index (regression constraint).
Text input surface. Some routes may not have a composer (e.g., empty thread).
Home screen container. Uses [role=main] with :has() as primary — this element only exists on home, not thread pages. Progressive rendering: home-icon appears first, utility bar can arrive 1-2s later.
CSS-compatible alias for home-route. Cannot use :has() in CSS, so this shorter selector is used in stylesheet rules. Same anchor element.
Home screen signal element. Stable testid across versions.
Suggestion/starter cards on home. Progressive rendering tolerance required.
Message content blocks. Can be 100+ per page — watch selector performance.
Code blocks and inline code elements.
Project selector dropdown. Only appears when projects are configured.

notes: Selector priority: data-testid > role/semantic tags > stable class name > CSS Modules prefix match. No exact hash. No pure structural paths.
CSS Modules prefix: match class*='_segmentName_' — the hash suffix varies per build, never match exact hashed classes.
Progressive rendering: L2 home anchors must tolerate late arrival — not found = skip refinement, never block L0/L1.
Cross-platform = version management: same-version DOMs are identical across platforms; upgrade Claude Code and re-verify against this contract.
CSS note: :has() is supported in modern Chromium (Electron embedded Chromium), but use shorter aliases in stylesheet rules for broader compatibility.
